suggested_requirements.text: The system must capture and manage files on assignment submission, forum, wiki, and announcement pages.
The system must allow for multiple file upload to be configured on a per-page basis.
Course administrators or professors shall enable multiple file uploads on a page during creation and editing stages.
The system must capture and organize voice clips.
The system must allow actors to organize their voice clips into a portfolio.
Equal and finite drive space shall be allotted to each actor in the role of professor or administrator for storing voice clips.
Course administrators or system administrators shall partition voice clip storage space for students.
The system shall allow actors to preview a voice clip before it is archived.
The system shall allow actors to attach archived voice clips to any page where uploads are permitted.
The system must allow actors to download their voice clips in MPEG Audio (mp3) format.
The system must store audio clips in a format optimized for speech.
The system shall provide a cross-platform viewer for listening to clips in Moodle.
The system must allow actors to delete recorded clips from their portfolio.
The system must display web feeds, such as RSS 2.0 feeds, for all pages where information blocks are added.
Course administrators shall determine which components have feeds and to whom those feeds pertain.
The system must allow web feeds to be turned on or off on a per-page basis.
An actor must be able to search through pages in a course.
The system shall provide a dedicated search page that allows actors to filter results by category and search specific sections.
The system must display a search box on every page after an actor has logged in.
A course administrator must be able to grade an assignment.
Course administrators shall post grades for an assignment based on the ratio of points earned to points possible.
The course administrator shall attach feedback in the form of text or an attachment to a grade.
The system shall attach timestamps to the last time a grade was modified.
The system should display grade information, averages, and overall grades to the actor to whom the grades belong.
No actor shall view another’s grades except for the course administrator for that course.
The system should maintain a history of grades for a particular assignment.
The system must provide a wiki where actors can collaboratively create networks of documents using a simple markup language.
The system must provide a blog engine supporting tagging, drafting, and comments.
The system must provide both e-mail and SMS notifications for pages.
Students shall select in their preferences whether notifications are sent via SMS or e-mail.
The system should provide a simple, responsive interface.
The system shall be configurable from a single source at a central administrative position.
The system must be backed up on a nightly basis.
The system must have the capacity to restore back-up data within six hours.
The system should be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
The system shall maintain 99% up-time.
The system should support at least 1000 concurrent users.
The system must be maintainable without substantial modification.
Relevant, online documentation for users should be available on each page.
System administrators must have access to a comprehensive, searchable database of maintenance tasks and help files.
